ledger.note: 3 August 1347: Calais surrenders to Edward III and becomes English. 'On 3 August 1347 Calais surrendered'; the siege began on 4 September 1346; 'The entire French population was expelled' and 'Edward repopulated the town with English settlers'. The Pale page: 'Calais was a prize of war won in the Battle of Crécy of 1346 by Edward III of England after a long siege.'

region.text: 'roughly encompassed the land between Gravelines and Wissant', about 20 square miles (52 km2)

ledger.note: 8 May 1360: the Treaty of Brétigny confirms English sovereignty and adds the land around Calais. 'English sovereignty was confirmed under the Treaty of Brétigny, signed on 8 May 1360'; Edward gave up his claim to the French throne in return for Aquitaine and 'the territory around Calais'. The page says the boundaries 'often changed and were ill-defined'; the Pale region is the extent 'between Gravelines and Wissant' (about 52 km2). The Treaty of Brétigny page has the treaty ratified at Calais on 24 October 1360.

ledger.note: 7 January 1558: the Duke of Guise takes Calais and the Pale is lost. 'On 1 January 1558' the French vanguard invested the area and Wentworth handed over the keys 'on 7 January'; 'The English defences of Guînes and Hames soon also fell'; France 'had reconquered the last territory it had lost in the Hundred Years' War'. The Pale page (infobox) gives 8 January 1558.

region.text: Calais and the Pale, taken by the Duke of Guise

ledger.note: January 1558: English rule in France ends. 'put an end to two centuries of fighting between England and France'; the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis (April 1559) kept Calais as an English possession in temporary French custody, with a price of 'half a million gold crowns' in eight years.

wars.name: Siege of Calais (1346-1347)
wars.outcome: Edward III took Calais on 3 August 1347 after the siege that began on 4 September 1346; the French population was expelled and the town became an English base for the rest of the Hundred Years' War and beyond.

wars.name: Siege of Calais (1558)
wars.outcome: The Duke of Guise took Calais in a week (1-7 January 1558); Guînes and Hames fell soon after, ending English rule in France.

certainty.note: The page says the Pale's boundaries 'often changed and were ill-defined' and the French kept retaking land, especially in the southwest.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from three pages (Pale of Calais, Siege of Calais 1346-1347, Siege of Calais 1558). The infobox area (about 52 km2, 'between Gravelines and Wissant') is far below the grid: the gazetteer region 'Pale of Calais' resolves to 6 cells (about 1,500 km2) and a 15 km disc round Calais to 2 cells (about 500 km2), the smallest the resolver returns, so the map overdraws the Pale by a factor of 10-30; the compile should draw it as a one- or two-cell exclave. Type colony of kingdom-of-england (family britain): the English Crown held it as an exclave, represented by the Calais constituency (no date given for 1536).
DATES: the Pale page's infobox gives the 1558 siege as 8 January, the siege page 1-7 January (keys handed over on 7 January); the Pale page gives 8 May 1360 for Brétigny, the Treaty of Brétigny page says drafted 8 or 10 May and ratified at Calais on 24 October 1360. Guînes and Hames fell soon after 7 January 1558; the page names no date for them and no captor.
NOT ON THE PAGES: the English Staple (1363), the 1436 siege, Guînes 1352-1360, the Spanish capture of 1596, the Pale's internal extent before 1360 (the 1347-1359 shape is only the town and its immediate land, a reading), who held the 'territory around Calais' before 1360.
The royal-domain-of-france dossier carries the matching 1558 gain with counterpart pale-of-calais (this dossier's slug) and the Kingdom of England dossier (eu-11) may carry the English side.
